author: Mistress Ulvasa Ralen
pages: Dreugh wax is not, as children in Ebonheart believe, a dreugh's earwax. It is the soft inner lining of the shell, shed and regrown each season, and prized by smiths and enchanters for what it does to metal and to magic.

The dreugh are not animals. They keep lairs, mounds of black rock on the sea bed with a single low mouth, and they guard them as a clan guards a hall. Where you find a mound you will find the brood's cast shells, and with them the wax.
Take only what is shed. Go in pairs, carry a water-breathing draught and a lamp, and never, ever linger near the largest lairs. The queens do not sleep.
